block.rationale: Fresh verification block. Lido WQ state at capture: lastRequestId=127194, lastFinalizedRequestId=127171, lastCheckpointIndex=1123. The two holders below together exercise both math branches (amountOfStETH for un-finalized, getClaimableEther for finalized) plus multi-request summing. amountOfStETH is fixed at request time, so the PRIMARY value is stable; the SECONDARY finalized request could be claimed by its owner at any time, which would zero its position (fine for a pinned fork block; re-verify before any live cross-check).

instance.note: Mainnet-only — Lido's WithdrawalQueueERC721 exists only on Ethereum. Standalone (non-meta) adapter. Denominated in native ETH (the asset Lido pays on claim; priced via ETH/USD, not stETH/USD, so a stETH depeg can't mis-value a claim that settles in full ETH). positionId = "" (account-global); protocolId = keccak256('lido-withdrawal'); positionKind = Supplied.

holders.label: PRIMARY
notes: Two PENDING (un-finalized, un-claimed) requests → valued via amountOfStETH (the redemption rate isn't fixed until finalization).
Exercises multi-request summing across an account.

legs_at_fork_block.ground_truth: sum of amountOfStETH across the account's open un-claimed un-finalized requests (getWithdrawalStatus)

holders.label: SECONDARY
notes: One FINALIZED, un-claimed request (id 127164) → valued via getClaimableEther (the exact claimable ETH, which after a negative rebase can be < amountOfStETH).

Here getClaimableEther == amountOfStETH == 54.619912948304940018 (normal case, no negative rebase) — the equality proves the finalized path resolves the checkpoint hint and reads the live claimable value correctly.

ground_truth.method: live WithdrawalQueueERC721 reads (NOT a Python re-derivation)
ground_truth.detail: Both branches are pinned against the real Lido WithdrawalQueue at the fork block. PRIMARY: oracle == sum of amountOfStETH over the open un-finalized requests. SECONDARY: oracle == getClaimableEther of the finalized request given its checkpoint hint. Plus protocolId == keccak256('lido-withdrawal'), positionId == "" (account-global), PositionKind.Supplied, balanceOracle == address(this), and the leg denominated in the native-ETH sentinel. The amountOfStETH-vs-getClaimableEther divergence (negative-rebase haircut) is covered with mocks in the unit test (test/balances/protocols/LidoWithdrawalQueueBalanceAdapter.t.sol).
